result.statement: The k=2 determinant layer for U(4) compresses exactly to a 3x3 doubly-stochastic complement-pair transport R plus an orientation matrix D with |D_ab|<=R_ab. For every support direction, its excess over actual S4 middle-layer permutation supports is bounded by an explicit three-coordinate parity defect depending only on spectra and support direction.
result.exact_middle_identity: L2=(1/2) sum_ab [R_ab Aplus_a Bplus_b + D_ab Aminus_a Bminus_b]
result.support_bound: Re(eta L2(U)) <= max_{rho in S3}(Hperm_rho + delta_rho), where delta_rho=0 unless the three orientation support coefficients have negative product, in which case delta_rho is their minimum absolute value.
result.full_determinant_interface: L1+L3 is an ordinary 4x4 bistochastic transport with the same one-minor matrix P; the unresolved target step is a joint scalar coupling inequality between P and (R,D) that absorbs the parity defect and forces one common S4 support optimizer.

cross_account_consumption.use: Consumed its exact rational orthogonal obstruction only as mathematical input showing that a spectrum-independent common permutation-marginal lift is too strong. No benchmark gold or unrelated data were consumed.

remaining_obligation: Derive a joint objective-level coupling inequality between the one-minor transport P and the complement-pair variables (R,D), or otherwise show the layer-1/3 slack pays delta_rho, for every spectra/support direction.
